verdict.reasoning: Patient reports shortness of breath starting over the last hour while sitting watching TV: "over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath" and confirmed it was while "sitting watching tv."
Shortness of breath started about an hour ago while at rest: "over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath" and this occurred "while you're sitting watching tv."

Patient notes palpitations/heart racing: "I feel like I'm getting really stressed out because, like, my heart is really going" and doctor clarifies "you're feeling your heart more than normal?" and patient replies "Yeah."
Patient denies chest pain at rest: In response to "does it cause any pain in your chest?" patient answers "No."
Chest soreness with deep inspiration: To "How about when you take a very deep breath in?" patient says "I mean, yeah, my chest feels sore..."
Patient reports C-section scar tenderness: same response also includes "but so does my C section scar. You know, it's all tender."
Cough started yesterday: "So I started with a cough yesterday."
No sputum production: To "Have you brought anything up?" patient replies "No, I haven't. No."

Patient is 4 weeks postpartum and currently with baby, but not that baby is at home: "Yeah. Four weeks." and "And are you with baby at the moment?" "Yes, I am." The fact incorrectly states the baby is at home.
Codeine used regularly post-op, stopped about a week ago: "They gave me some codeine." and "Yeah, I've been taking that fairly regularly, but probably haven't taken it for a week."
Allergy to ibuprofen with unknown reaction: "I'm allergic to ibuprofen, though." and to "what happens when you take ibuprofen?" patient answers "I don't know."
Maternal history of leg clots: "my mum's had clots in her legs before."
Partner at work: "Is anyone else with you at home?" "No, my partner's at work."
Self-counted 30 heartbeats: after timed count, "How many did you count?" patient says "I counted 30."
Clinician notes slightly fast heart rate: "Good. So your heart is running slightly fast at the moment..." which indicates tachycardia.

No vitals/physical exam/investigations documented beyond pulse count. Transcript contains no blood pressure, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, formal exam findings, or tests, so stating none documented is consistent with the record.
Acute dyspnea with sudden onset at rest matches: "over the last hour, I've started to feel, like, a bit short of breath" while "sitting watching tv."

Pulmonary embolism/clot considered due to recent C-section: "given that you've had a C section... some people can suffer with clots, and those can either be found in the legs or... your chest. So in your lungs." This is a PE/VTE concern four weeks postpartum.

Tachycardia and palpitations seen as likely reactive but needing assessment: "your heart is running slightly fast at the moment, which is probably because of your shortness of breath and some of the pain that you're under" and plan for hospital assessment confirms need for evaluation.
Nonproductive cough for one day: "So I started with a cough yesterday" and "Have you brought anything up?" "No, I haven't. No."

Postpartum state after C-section with VTE risk and recent opioid use: "I had a C section a few weeks ago"/"Yeah. Four weeks." plus discussion of clots as a risk, and "They gave me some codeine" with regular use until a week ago.
Allergy to ibuprofen: "I'm allergic to ibuprofen, though."

Advised urgent hospital/ED evaluation and patient chose to self-present with baby after declining ambulance: "it might be worth you going into the hospital to get checked out a bit further"; "I can call an ambulance or you can take yourself"; patient: "I'll go. I'll take myself." and "you can take yourself to the hospital with baby."
Told to go quickly and bring baby supplies: "what I would suggest is go fairly quickly and take some bits for baby at the same time."
Advised to hold codeine: "if you're taking any medications, like codeine, don't take them for the time being."
There is no mention of the clinician planning to call or communicate with the emergency department; only advice for the patient to attend hospital is documented.
No explicit safety-net advice about calling an ambulance or returning if symptoms worsen is documented beyond the immediate plan to go to hospital now.
